entry.title: [HIGH] Write can overwrite unread existing files on Claude 5 models.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.238 macOS repro found that Claude 5 family models can use the Write tool to replace an existing file that was never read in the conversation, while older models still fail with the previous read-before-overwrite guard. In a shared-file workflow, a fresh session can therefore replace another session's recent entries without first seeing them, and the Write tool's own prompt text may still describe the old guard as if the overwrite should fail. The behavior is documented in the tools reference but easy to discover only after data loss.

entry.title: [HIGH] PermissionRequest hooks can be skipped in print mode.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.237 Windows repro found that `PermissionRequest` hooks did not fire during a non-interactive `claude -p` Write request, even though a `PreToolUse` hook from the same settings file, same matcher, and same script fired normally for the same tool. The command and HTTP PermissionRequest variants both produced no hook log entry, leaving the model to ask for an approval that cannot be answered in print mode. This makes the hook event unreliable for its most automation-relevant path: headless runs where a hook-supplied decision is the only way to answer a prompt.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bypass mode can steer file work away from typed tools into composed shell strings.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.228 through 2.1.235 behavior found that sessions running in bypass permissions mode receive a built-in instruction to do file reads, searches, and edits through Bash commands such as `cat`, `grep`, `sed`, heredocs, or short scripts where possible, rather than the dedicated Read, Grep, Edit, or Write tools. The reporter tied this to observed composition failures including laundered pipeline exit statuses, broken nested quoting, broad `git add -A` staging, backtick execution inside quoted command bodies, and POSIX awk portability mismatches. Because bypass mode is often used for unattended or headless work, this prompt-level steering can replace typed tool arguments with one-shot shell strings exactly when there may be no human watching the transcript.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Auto mode can execute assistant-authored destructive scripts without seeing hidden effects.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code auto-mode WSL2 session destroyed the user's home directory after the assistant wrote a Bash helper containing a cleanup trap, later changed the variable referenced by that trap, and then executed the script. The permission check saw only a surface command like `bash /tmp/.../test-lib-demo.sh`, not the destructive behavior now hidden inside a file the assistant had authored earlier in the same session. The report ties this to several earlier destructive deletion incidents and highlights a broader write-then-execute gap: permission decisions can inspect the command string while missing dangerous behavior embedded in assistant-created code.

entry.title: [HIGH] Worktree Bash guard can block git-free commands.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.235 macOS worktree-isolated session saw the built-in Bash guard refuse ordinary multi-step shell commands with a message about unverifiable worktree git operations even when the command had no git token and no path outside the worktree. A later Linux 2.1.238 matrix narrowed the behavior: some compound forms are allowed, but simple loops, assignments, and variable-expanded reads can still be false positives, while `bash -c 'git -C <main> ...'` was allowed and ran against the main checkout. A larger local transcript corpus then found 2,628 such refusals across 591 of 12,623 sessions, with 73.2% of matched refused commands containing no git token and 274 refusals involving the session scratchpad the harness itself instructed agents to use.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] User PreToolUse hooks can miss Bash calls inside Task-spawned subagents.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.234 setup found that a user-level `PreToolUse` hook for Bash fired in the top-level session but did not run for Bash calls issued by Task-spawned subagents. The same hook binary accepted a hand-built payload and returned a valid rewrite response, and direct top-level Bash calls still logged as expected, so the narrowed failure is the subagent execution surface losing hook coverage. Users can reasonably believe a user-scope Bash guard, rewrite, or audit hook covers every Bash execution path, while delegated work may run raw commands with no hook invocation.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bio safeguards can hard-block base64 file verification.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code desktop session doing ordinary Markdown file editing and byte-verification work was flagged by the `[bio]` safeguard after base64 file-comparison steps, then later hard-blocked plain-English and grep-only follow-up turns in the same conversation. The report includes request IDs for two hard blocks and suggests the classifier may be scoring accumulated connector/tool context, including large opaque base64 blobs, rather than only the current user message. For agentic coding sessions this turns benign file-integrity work into a persistent session-level interruption where the user may need to rebuild context in a new conversation.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows project path spelling can split trust, MCP, and worktree state.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code setup found that `.claude.json` can store the same project directory under multiple raw path spellings, such as lowercase-drive forward-slash, uppercase-drive forward-slash, and uppercase-drive backslash forms. Those records did not carry equivalent state: the backslash spelling held `hasTrustDialogAccepted: true`, while forward-slash records held MCP server and active worktree fields but had trust unset. The visible result is a project that appears to lose configured MCP servers, forget active worktree state, or re-prompt for trust, even though all records refer to the same directory.

entry.title: [HIGH] Desktop bundled @inline plugins can re-enable after restart.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop Cowork setup found that bundled `@inline` plugins such as marketing and product-management could not be disabled persistently. Disabling them in the app UI or setting `enabledPlugins` entries to `false` in `~/.claude/settings.json` survived on disk, but after each Desktop restart the bundled plugin skill sets and MCP servers were enabled again. Because these plugins are bundled inside the Desktop app rather than ordinary installed plugins, `claude plugin list` and the local plugin cache did not show a removable or inspectable source of truth. The result is silent reintroduction of about 65 skills and related plugin context into sessions where the user believed those plugins were off.

entry.title: [HIGH] Worktree `git -C` path classifier can invert safe and unsafe targets.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.228 worktree-isolated session found that the built-in git command safety check classified `git -C <path>` by the path token's leading character rather than by the directory it resolves to. Literal in-worktree targets such as `git -C .` and `git -C ./tmp/some-clone ...` were refused as unverifiable runtime computations, while `git -C "$HOME/some-other-repo" ...` was allowed and executed against a repository outside the isolated worktree. The refusal is a hard tool error rather than a permission prompt, so users cannot approve a safe in-worktree false positive from the normal dialog path.

entry.title: [HIGH] PostToolUse rewrite collisions can silently drop redactions.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.234 repro found that when multiple `PostToolUse` hooks return conflicting `hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput` values for the same tool call, the winning rewrite is deterministic by registration order rather than by completion order. In the repro, a later-registered identity rewrite restored the original Bash output after an earlier redaction hook masked a recognizable secret, so the model received the unmasked value. Claude Code emitted no warning that one rewrite had clobbered another, and the relevant SDK warning was attached to `classifierContext` rather than the `updatedToolOutput` field that carries the security-sensitive replacement.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Automatic worktree cleanup can delete active session directories.
entry.summary: A reported macOS Claude Code setup found that an unattended worktree cleanup path removed `.claude/worktrees/<name>` directories while live sessions were still using them, including one deletion during a Bash tool call whose cwd was the removed worktree. Three unrelated concurrent sessions lost worktree directories within about ten minutes. The common git-state fingerprint was a clean worktree whose branch tip was already an ancestor of `origin/main`, which is a valid signal that the contents are captured elsewhere but not a valid liveness check for whether a session is still reading, planning, or about to write there.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Daemon worker can delete symlinked settings.json.
entry.summary: A reported Nix/home-manager Claude Code 2.1.219 setup found that a long-lived daemon-hosted `claude bg-spare` worker repeatedly unlinked `~/.claude/settings.json` when that path was a symlink into a read-only store directory. Kernel audit records attributed four successful `unlinkat` deletions to the same idle Claude Code worker within 7 to 69 seconds of the symlink being recreated, while replacing the symlink with a regular file stopped the deletion. Because `settings.json` carries permissions, hooks, sandbox policy, model, env, and status line, this can silently drop every user-level guardrail and make later sessions fall back to defaults with no obvious UI error.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows plugin hook command rewrites can report false success.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Claude Code 2.1.220 setup found that already-installed plugin hook commands were rewritten from a Bash `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` form into an absolute `cmd /d /s /c ...run-hook.cmd` command while the hook still declared `"shell": "bash"`. Bash then launched a bare interactive `cmd`, the hook's JSON stdin was echoed into the Windows prompt, and Claude Code recorded the result as `hook_success` with the Windows banner injected as hook context. The reporter classified 119 local session transcripts and found the plugin SessionStart context missing from most sessions across roughly a month, with clean installs later re-mangled by another rewrite.

entry.title: [HIGH] Marketplace-entry dependencies can be ignored by graph consumers.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.237 plugin-marketplace repro found that dependencies declared on a marketplace entry were used by install-time name resolution but not by the rest of the dependency graph. Version constraints such as `~2.1.0` could silently resolve to an incompatible newer tag, conflicting ranges were not reported, `list --json` showed no dependency errors, and `uninstall <unrelated> --prune -y` removed an auto-installed dependency that the dependent plugin still needed. Declaring the same edge in the dependent plugin's own `plugin.json` made version checks, disable/enable behavior, and prune protection work.

entry.title: [HIGH] Hook stdin EOF can hang synchronous hook sessions.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Claude Code 2.1.208 and later setup found that synchronous hook processes can intermittently receive a written JSON payload without the client closing the hook stdin pipe. Hook code that waits for EOF, such as `json.load(sys.stdin)`, then blocks forever, and because the hook is synchronous the whole session freezes until the specific child hook process is killed. The reporter reproduced it under hook-heavy Bash workflows and noted that killing only the hung hook process lets the session resume, pointing to hook stdin lifecycle handling rather than model latency.

entry.title: [HIGH] Desktop remote plugin sync can omit plugin hooks.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop remote SSH session passed synced plugin directories under `~/.claude/remote/plugins` to the remote `ccd-cli`, but those synced copies omitted each plugin's `hooks/` directory and `hooks/hooks.json`. The same plugin's skills and commands worked, direct `settings.json` hooks fired in the desktop remote session, and a control `--plugin-dir` pointing at a complete plugin registered hooks normally. This means a plugin-delivered `PreToolUse` guard can appear enabled in a desktop remote session while its hook dispatch path is silently absent.

entry.title: [HIGH] Flagged tool-output content can leak into a later tool-call input.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Claude Code 2.1.237 session produced a malformed `Read` tool call whose `file_path` began like a truncated local path and then contained roughly 900 words of injected content, including Claude Code's own wrapper phrase for suspicious tool output and fake instructions to exfiltrate data. The permission prompt intercepted the malformed call and the user rejected it before execution, but the wrapper phrase appearing inside a new tool input suggests previously flagged content may have crossed from inert tool output into tool-call argument construction.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Worktree command safety can misread builtin names as invocations.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 worktree-isolated session found that Claude Code's Bash command-safety analyzer refused commands containing shell builtin names such as `complete`, `compgen`, or `compopt` even when those words appeared as ordinary non-leading arguments. The concrete failure was a Python workflow command whose subcommand was named `complete`; the analyzer treated the argument as if Bash would invoke the completion builtin and refused it as unverifiable inside the worktree. Quoting the token and disabling the sandbox did not help because the refusal came from the PreToolUse-layer worktree analyzer, not from the sandbox.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Desktop can hide Auto mode despite defaultMode settings.
entry.summary: A reported personal Claude Max macOS Desktop session stopped offering Auto in the Claude Code permission-mode picker and labelled bypass permissions as disabled by the user's organization, even though the account had no managed policy and `~/.claude/settings.json` still set `permissions.defaultMode` to `auto`. The same machine's terminal CLI continued to start in Auto mode, so the regression appeared isolated to Desktop-started sessions or Desktop remote configuration rather than the local settings file.
